linkedin.title: Most news feeds are broken because they treat everyone like the same person.
linkedin.body:
We have all been there. You click on one article about a tech launch, and suddenly your entire feed is nothing but tech press releases for the next three weeks. It is not helpful. It is just noise.

At Headlinne, we realized that personalization should not be about predicting what you might click on next. It should be about understanding the topics you actually value. A good recommendation engine does not just look at your clicks. It looks at the depth of your interest.

When we built our system, we focused on nuance. If you read a piece about renewable energy, the engine should not just dump every article with the word 'energy' in the headline onto your screen. It should learn whether you care about the policy side, the investment angle, or the consumer technology behind it.

True personalization happens when the app gets quieter, not louder. It learns to filter out the fluff so you can focus on the stories that actually inform your day.

slides.headline: Science News You Can Use
slides.subtitle: From space mysteries to ancient predators, here is your quick science briefing.

slides.headline: Mapping the building blocks of stars
slides.explanation: Scientists are using radio telescopes to track exactly how molecules evolve in space. This research helps explain how the raw materials of the universe eventually turn into planets and people.

slides.headline: Japan targets Mars' moons
slides.explanation: Japan is preparing a space mission to retrieve samples from the moons of Mars. These rocks could hold the secrets to how the solar system formed and how life began on Earth.

slides.headline: A star with black hole energy
slides.explanation: Astronomers found an object in the early universe that looks like a star but emits massive amounts of energy. It is so bright that it defies our current understanding of how stars produce power.

slides.headline: Greek island fire update
slides.explanation: Firefighters are working for a second day to contain a forest blaze on the island of Skyros. Local officials are optimistic that the situation will be under control soon.

slides.headline: Ancient giants of South America
slides.explanation: Fossil evidence shows that giant crocodylians once ruled a massive lake in South America over 10 million years ago. This discovery paints a picture of a continent dominated by massive prehistoric predators.

instagram.caption:
Science is constantly shifting our understanding of the world around us.

From deep space discoveries to ancient history right here on Earth, there is always something new to learn. Which of these stories did you find the most interesting?
